reference.source: Zuikaku as at Leyte Gulf, October 1944. lengthM (257.5 m / 844 ft 10 in overall), flightDeck.lengthM and widthM (242.2 m / 794 ft 7 in, 29 m / 95 ft 2 in maximum width), 9.32 m deep-load draft and the ten transverse arrestor wires are from the English Wikipedia article 'Shokaku-class aircraft carrier', read 2026-10-11; maxSpeedMps is its 34.5 kn designed speed. The original Blender model's hull stations, island, three elevators, funnel, masts, AA galleries and camouflage were measured from Wikimedia Commons 'Fig of japanese aircraft carrier Zuikaku in 1944.gif' (SnowCloudInSummer, CC BY-SA 3.0, read 2026-10-11; the file cites Nihon Kaigun Kantei Zumenshu, 4th ed. (1978), and Shashin Nihon no Gunkan vol. 3 (1989)); the measurement table and every estimate are in tools/models/blender/zuikaku-cv.py. deckWidthM is the flight deck's 29 m. beamM (26 m) is an ESTIMATE of the waterline beam: the article gives only the 29 m overall beam. flightDeck.heightM and deckHeightM are the SAME ESTIMATE at 15.5 m / 51 ft above the waterline, kept because the simulation's deck, trap and landing tuning use it. trapZone is an ESTIMATE laid over the ten wires aft, scaled from essex-cv's. paddles, turnRateRadPerS and hullHp are essex-cv's, so the two carriers play alike: CHOICES, not history. ARMAMENT, CHOSEN FOR BALANCE AGAINST essex-cv (M1d D3), NOT HISTORY: the eight twin 12.7 cm Type 89 dual-purpose mounts are real (two pairs a side on modeled hull sponsons) and carried as turrets with aa: heavy, as essex-cv carries its 5-inch. Light AA is four triple 25 mm Type 96 mounts, two a side, on modeled deck-edge tubs nearest the island and aft. The real 1944 fit after the Philippine Sea was 20 triple and 36 single 25 mm (96 barrels) and eight 28-round 12 cm AA rocket launchers (same article, Armament, citing Lengerer and Campbell).
